findings_addressed: IMPORTANT #1 (payoff-timing narrative contradicted by the data): Reframed the whole proposal. I no longer sell this as a likely conversion win via 'payoff moment'. The report, changelog and PR body now state the honest prior — a secondary link below the share CTA on the path to the ~0-converting preview page most plausibly converts ~0, like preview/share, NOT like the captive full-screen in-app thank-you. The stated durable value is (a) making the surface tracked and (b) correct-per-product ASIN routing. measurable:false kept.

IMPORTANT #2 (correct-ASIN benefit depends on an unverified master_products/ROS-env dependency; a null sku or unreachable lookup routes EVERY non-potato buyer to the potato listing): I EMPIRICALLY verified the dependency by booting the app and hitting /api/product-lookup for the top SKUs — all returned 404 (master_products is unreachable with this deploy's env). I cannot configure deploy env (out of scope) so, rather than ship a potato-for-everyone version, I made resolution robust WITHOUT the ROS env: review-redirect now resolves ASIN by precedence asin -> sku(master_products, when present) -> a self-contained character map (byte-for-byte the same ASINs the live in-app links use) -> default. resolve-video.js passes both sku AND character. Verified locally that cupcake->B0DVGVHSZV and nursePotato->B0DFMXPQKH resolve correctly even with master_products unreachable, so the realistic behaviour is NOT fallback-to-potato for non-potato buyers. The remaining ROS-env dependency (needed only for products beyond potato/cupcake/nursePotato) is reported as a deploy dependency, not silently assumed. I also fixed a latent bug found while building: the original outer time-cap would have defaulted to potato if the DB call merely hung — I moved the cap to wrap only the DB call so a slow/failed lookup always falls through to the character map.

MINOR #3 (receiver-heavy audience is an available headwind, not undeterminable): Acknowledged. The role split is ~73% receiver among identified roles this window; receivers who did not buy on Amazon cannot leave a verified-purchase review, which caps the ceiling. Folded into the honest expected-value framing.
MINOR #4 (reach overstated as 'opened by ~36'): Corrected to 'sent to ~36' (video_created = emails sent, not opens) and present the +20-40% as an optimistic ceiling, not an expectation.

change.title: Add a gentle 'leave an honest review' link to the video-ready email
change.targets: Post-video review capture — the 'your video is ready' delivery email, which previously had no review ask and no tracking.
change.expected_effect: The delivery email now offers a warm, tracked path to leave an honest Amazon review, landing on the correct product. Most likely this converts about as well as the preview/share links (i.e. very few clicks) — the real, reliable win is that these clicks are now measured and go to the right product listing. Not expected to show a provable change at this traffic.
change.why_it_helps: Every customer who finishes a video gets an email to watch it, but that email never invited them to leave a review — so a warm moment was going unused and unmeasured. Now there's a soft, optional 'leave an honest review' link that also sends them to the exact product they bought.
changes_in_plain_words: The 'your video is ready' email now has a small, friendly line underneath the main button inviting the customer to leave an honest review — no pressure, and never tied to the discount.
That review link now sends people to the correct product's Amazon page (the cupcake buyer lands on the cupcake, not always the potato), using the same product info the in-app screen already uses.
Every click on that link is now counted, so from next cycle we can actually see whether this email produces reviews (before, it produced and recorded nothing).
The existing reminder-email review links are completely unchanged — they behave exactly as before.
change.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: Review clicks are near-entirely produced by the one prominent ask on the in-app thank-you screen — which is a captive, full-screen 'leave a review while you wait' interstitial the user is parked on during generation, not a payoff moment. Every other surface either had no ask (delivery email) or an already-prominent-but-ignored one (preview/share). The delivery email offered no path to act on any goodwill at all.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A meaningful share of delivery-email recipients are buyers able to leave a verified-purchase review (not only gift receivers) — and the audience is in fact ~73% receiver among identified roles, a real headwind on the ceiling.

sku and/or character are present on the video_sessions row at send time so the correct ASIN resolves (character map covers potato/cupcake/nursePotato even without the master_products lookup; other products need the ROS Supabase env).
A secondary review link does not pull people away from 'Watch & Share' enough to reduce sharing/recipient reach (watch share_completed and share_page_opened).
'Honest review' framing (Amazon TOS) reads as warm, not cold, and the discount is never linked to reviewing.
change.second_order_effects: The email's primary purpose is to get the creator to watch and SHARE (share -> recipient opens video.html -> reach). The review link stays visually secondary and below the unchanged primary CTA, so share risk is minimal and watchable via share_completed. Routing through review-redirect means these clicks now also mark the Klaviyo profile review_clicked=true and land in Supabase as phase=email_redirect/source=video_email, making the surface measurable for future cycles.
change.strongest_case_against: The delivery-email audience is receiver-heavy (~73% of identified roles); receivers can't leave verified-purchase reviews, so a payoff-moment ask likely converts near zero and you've added a line to a working share email. And the audit is right that this secondary-link-to-preview-page shape resembles the ~0-converting preview/share asks, not the captive thank-you that works. Answer: (1) the ask is secondary and below the unchanged primary CTA, so share risk is minimal and monitored; (2) the change's DEFENSIBLE value does not depend on conversion at all — it makes a previously-invisible surface tracked and fixes an untracked/wrong-ASIN review path; (3) it is explicitly measurable:false — no 'worked' claim will ever be made without a SIGNIFICANT result.

tradeoff.gained: A tracked, correctly-targeted honest-review link on the highest-reach post-video surface we control (sent to ~36 finishers/fortnight), plus fixing an untracked/wrong-ASIN review path — directly serving the objective (reviews), and making the surface measurable from next cycle.
tradeoff.risked: Preview/share behaviour could dip slightly if the secondary link distracts from 'Watch & Share'; baseline to watch is share_completed = 9 this window (9 prior) and share_page_opened = 21 (19 prior). The Klaviyo reminder-email review path (source=email) is untouched, so that channel is unaffected.
unverified_assumptions: Whether delivery-email recipients are predominantly buyers (verified-review-eligible) or receivers — the role split leans receiver (~73% of identified), an adverse-but-imperfect signal.

Whether the ROS Supabase env (ROS_SUPABASE_*) is configured in the live deploy — verified NOT present in this cycle's env (all product-lookups 404). Products beyond potato/cupcake/nursePotato therefore fall back to potato until that env is configured; the top-3 products resolve correctly regardless via the self-contained character map.

Whether B0DK1RF3TZ in the dead send-video-email.js was ever intentional (a flagship/brand ASIN) — owner should confirm the canonical review ASIN logic; I align to the maintained in-app per-product resolution.

change.differs_from_past_attempt: Not PR #8 (claim-page layout — untouched). Not the owner-rejected discount-before-email or printed-number moves (no claim-page or discount change). Not the June preview/share prominence rework (different surface — the delivery email; and I am ADDING an ask where none existed, not re-running 'make the existing ask more prominent'). Not the Klaviyo Email 5/6 reminders (out of scope, untouched) — this is the repo-owned Resend delivery email.

Empirically confirmed the audit's dependency concern: /api/product-lookup returned 404 for all top SKUs (no ROS env here), which is exactly why the self-contained character map was added. pr_body:
## What this does

The email we send when a customer's video is ready ("Your Video is Ready!") is opened by everyone who finishes a video — but it only ever said "Watch & Share" and never invited them to leave a review. This adds a small, warm, optional **"Leave an honest review"** link underneath the main button. The link now (a) is **counted**, so we can finally see whether this email produces any reviews, and (b) sends people to the **correct product's** Amazon page — the cupcake buyer lands on the cupcake listing, not always the potato.

The wording follows Amazon's rules ("honest review", never tied to the discount) and the owner's design bar (secondary, subdued, warm, no pushiness — the "Watch & Share" button stays the one main action).

## Verdict on the last change (2026-07-06 message-step fix)

**Still not yet measurable.** On steady traffic the warm-user step "gave email → started a video" read 37.5% (24 of 64) before and 44.6% (29 of 65) after — a +7.1 point move, but the significance test says this is **indistinguishable from noise** (p = 0.41; you'd need ~750 people per two-week window to call a 7-point change, we have ~64). The independent auditor reran the numbers and agreed. This is a respected "pending" verdict, not a failure — at this traffic almost nothing this small can be proven either way.

## The biggest leaks right now

1. **The email gate on the claim page** (~56% of scanners never give an email) — the largest loss, but this cycle it has only spent ground (the layout redesign already came out flat) or owner-rejected ideas left, so it is not a clean thing to ship.
2. **Post-video review capture** (chosen) — all 10 review clicks this window came from the one in-app screen; the delivery email, preview and share screens produced zero. The delivery email in particular had **no review link at all** and wasn't tracked.
3. **Warm users who don't finish a video** — this is the step the last change targeted and it's still cooling, so touching it now would spoil that measurement.

## What the auditor said, and how I responded

The auditor approved the idea but asked for two corrections before building:

- **"Don't oversell this as a conversion win."** Fair. The one review ask that works is a captive full-screen screen the user is parked on while their video generates — not a "payoff moment." A secondary link that leads to the preview page more likely behaves like the preview/share links, which convert ~0. So I've framed the honest value as **tracking + correct product routing**, not a conversion win. It's explicitly marked unmeasurable — I will never claim it "worked" without a statistically solid result.
- **"Prove the correct-product link actually works, or it silently sends everyone to the potato."** I checked: in this environment the product-lookup database is unreachable (every lookup returned "not found"), which would indeed have sent every non-potato buyer to the potato page. So instead of relying on that lookup, I built a **self-contained backup** using the exact same product→page mapping the in-app screen already uses. Verified locally that a cupcake buyer now correctly lands on the cupcake page even with the database unreachable. Full coverage for less-common products still needs one piece of deploy configuration (the ROS database credentials) — flagged below as a dependency, not silently assumed.
- Two smaller notes: the audience skews ~73% gift-receivers (who often can't leave a verified-purchase review — a real ceiling), and "~36" is emails **sent**, not opened. Both folded into the honest expectations.

## How I verified it

Ran the app locally and clicked through the review link with every product and every edge case: cupcake, nurse-potato and potato all resolve to the right Amazon page; unknown products fall back safely; the existing reminder-email links behave exactly as before; a bad/injected value is ignored. Rendered the email and confirmed the new link shows below the main button. Cleaned up all 27 test records afterward. (Screenshots couldn't be captured — no browser tool in this environment — so I saved before/after email HTML for comparison instead.)

## What to re-measure, and when

Around **2026-08-11** (needs 2–3 weeks of data), check review clicks tagged `source=video_email`, and confirm sharing (`share_completed`, `share_page_opened`) didn't dip. Any effect will almost certainly be too small to prove at this traffic — that's expected and fine.

## Deploy dependency for the owner

For products **beyond** potato/cupcake/nurse-potato to route to the exactly-right Amazon page, the live site needs the ROS database credentials (`ROS_SUPABASE_URL` / key) configured — the same ones the in-app review links already rely on. Without them, those less-common products fall back to the potato page (just like the in-app screen does today); the top three products are always correct.
telegram_summary: Last change (Jul-6 message fix): still NOT provable — 37.5%->44.6% but p=0.41, pure noise at this traffic (auditor agreed). Top leaks: claim-page email gate (blocked this cycle), then post-video review capture (chosen). Shipped: the 'your video is ready' email now has a warm, optional 'leave an honest review' link — tracked, and pointing to the correct product's Amazon page (cupcake buyer -> cupcake, not potato). Honest note per the audit: this likely converts like the preview/share links (~0); the real win is it's now measured and correctly targeted, not a conversion claim. Marked unmeasurable. Reminder emails untouched.
